title: Daler Mehndi Thanks Mika Singh in Diwali Message After Uttarakhand Stage Row
excerpt: Three weeks after a Uttarakhand minister interrupted his live show and alleged he was intoxicated and lip-syncing — allegations his family denies — Daler Mehndi used a Diwali Instagram note to thank his brother, his family and the industry for standing by him.
body:
• Daler Mehndi posted a long Diwali message on Instagram on Sunday, November 8, thanking fans, family and the music industry — his first extended public statement since the October 18 Uttarakhand concert row.
  • "My brother Mika stood up for me like a force to reckon with," he wrote, also thanking his wife Taran, son Gurdeep and daughters Rabab, Ajit and Prabhjot.
  • At the October 18 fair performance in New Tehri, Uttarakhand cabinet minister Subodh Uniyal interrupted the show and alleged Mehndi appeared intoxicated and was not singing live — allegations Mika Singh has denied, saying Mehndi does not drink and had recently undergone surgery.
  • The two sides still dispute whether Uniyal apologised: Mika's team said he did so by phone; Uniyal has denied apologising. Uttarakhand Chief Minister Pushkar Singh Dhami has spoken to both sides urging harmony.

Daler Mehndi has broken his silence on the Uttarakhand concert controversy — with a Diwali message of thanks rather than a rebuttal. In a long Instagram note posted on Sunday, the singer wished fans "Happy Diwali to you and your loved ones" and thanked his family, the music industry and the public for what he called "this Saropao of love, faith and respect."

"My brother Mika stood up for me like a force to reckon with."

— Daler Mehndi, Diwali Instagram message

"My family has been my greatest strength through this time," Mehndi wrote, thanking his wife Taran for "her courage and unwavering belief," his son Gurdeep for his resilience and his daughters Rabab, Ajit and Prabhjot for their unconditional love. He invoked Ik Onkar — the Sikh teaching that all are one — and said he felt fortunate to witness in his lifetime the love that artists usually only hear about after they are gone. The diyas, he wrote, will shine in every home, but "the light that your love has ignited in my heart is the most special to me."

What happened in New Tehri

The message closes a three-week public dispute. On October 18, during Mehndi's live performance at the Siddhpeeth Maa Kunjapuri Tourism and Development Fair in New Tehri, Uttarakhand, state cabinet minister Subodh Uniyal walked onto the stage, interrupted the performance and publicly questioned it. Uniyal alleged that Mehndi appeared intoxicated and was not singing live, despite reportedly being paid Rs 35 lakh for the show, according to the Times of India. No independent or medical verification of the intoxication allegation has been reported.

Mika Singh led the defence of his elder brother. He said Mehndi does not drink, noted that the singer had recently undergone surgery, and demanded an apology from the minister. Other industry figures, including Rajpal Yadav, Shaan, Kapil Sharma and Anupam Kher, cited Mehndi's ill health in his support.

An apology both sides describe differently

Whether the matter was settled remains disputed. Mika Singh's team circulated a statement saying Uniyal had apologised by phone: "We appreciate that Subodh Uniyal ji has apologised to Daler Mehndi paaji over a telephonic conversation regarding the unfortunate incident." Uniyal has denied apologising. "There is no question of me apologising," he said, asking, "Have I committed any crime that I should apologise?" He also argued that if Mehndi was unwell, he should have declined the show or told the organisers and audience. Uttarakhand Chief Minister Pushkar Singh Dhami intervened, speaking to both Mika Singh and Mehndi and conveying the government's wish to move past the episode in a spirit of harmony. Mehndi's Diwali note does not mention the minister or the allegations directly — it thanks the people who stood by him, and stops there.
